### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

The following mlir for standard Flash Attention might not use all vector cores. How can I improve it? The biggest difference with [pto-isa fa_performance kernel ](https://gitcode.com/cann/pto-isa/blob/master/kernels/manual/common/flash_atten/fa_performance_kernel.cpp?init=initTree)is the lack of `TMpipe` and `subblock` indexing for vector cores, which I tried to implement without success due to probably the lack of entry_offset for `TPush` and `Tpop` in the dialect.
Here you can find the [PTO-DSL](https://github.com/huawei-csl/pto-dsl/pull/112) code that generates the following MLIR.

### Reproduction (minimal)

```mlir

    %13 = arith.cmpi slt, %3, %5 : index

    %16 = arith.addi %4, %c1 : index
    %17 = arith.select %15, %16, %4 : index
    %18 = arith.addi %14, %17 : index
    %c65536 = arith.constant 65536 : index
    %19 = arith.muli %3, %c65536 : index
    %20 = pto.addptr %arg0, %19 : <f32> -> <f32>
    %21 = pto.import_reserved_buffer{name = "fa_c2v_fifo", peer_func = @vector_kernel} -> i32

      pto.tload ins(%37 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x32xf16>) outs(%23 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x32xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>)

      pto.tload ins(%38 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x256xf16>) outs(%25 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>)
      pto.tmov ins(%25 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>) outs(%26 : !pto.tile_buf<right, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>)
      pto.tmatmul ins(%24, %26 : !pto.tile_buf<left, 32x32xf16, slayout=row_major>, !pto.tile_buf<right, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>) outs(%27 : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x256xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>)
      pto.tpush_to_aiv(%27 : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x256xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>) {split = 0}
      %39 = pto.partition_view %35, offsets = [%c0, %c0], sizes = [%c256, %c32_0] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<256x32xf16>
      pto.tload ins(%39 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<256x32xf16>) outs(%30 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 256x32xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>)
      scf.for %arg5 = %c1 to %c32_1 step %c1 {
        %41 = arith.muli %arg5, %c256 : index
        %42 = pto.partition_view %34, offsets = [%c0, %41], sizes = [%c32_0, %c256] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x256xf16>
        pto.tload ins(%42 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x256xf16>) outs(%25 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>)
        %43 = pto.tpop_from_aiv {split = 0} -> !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x256xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>

        %44 = pto.partition_view %35, offsets = [%41, %c0], sizes = [%c256, %c32_0] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<256x32xf16>
        pto.tload ins(%44 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<256x32xf16>) outs(%30 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 256x32xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>)
        pto.tmatmul ins(%29, %31 : !pto.tile_buf<left, 32x256xf16, slayout=row_major>, !pto.tile_buf<right, 256x32xf16, slayout=col_major>) outs(%32 : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x32xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>)
        pto.tpush_to_aiv(%32 : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x32xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>) {split = 0}
        pto.tmov ins(%25 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>) outs(%26 : !pto.tile_buf<right, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>)
        pto.tmatmul ins(%24, %26 : !pto.tile_buf<left, 32x32xf16, slayout=row_major>, !pto.tile_buf<right, 32x256xf16, slayout=col_major>) outs(%27 : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x256xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>)
        pto.tpush_to_aiv(%27 : !pto.tile_buf<acc, 32x256xf32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024>) {split = 0}
      }

      pto.tmov ins(%40 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 32x256xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>) outs(%29 : !pto.tile_buf<left, 32x256xf16, slayout=row_major>)

      pto.tmov ins(%30 : !pto.tile_buf<mat, 256x32xf16, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major>) outs(%31 : !pto.tile_buf<right, 256x32xf16, slayout=col_major>)

    %21 = pto.reserve_buffer{name = "fa_c2v_fifo", size = 32768, location = <vec>, auto = true} -> i32
```

To reproduce, the generated cpp requires some manual fixes. See the perl lines in this shell script:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ARTIFACT_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/build_artifacts"
MLIR_PATH="${ARTIFACT_DIR}/fa_gen.mlir"
GENERATED_CPP="${ARTIFACT_DIR}/fa_gen.cpp"
LIB_PATH="${ARTIFACT_DIR}/fa_lib.so"

PTO_LIB_PATH="${PTO_LIB_PATH:-/sources/pto-isa}"

mkdir -p "${ARTIFACT_DIR}"
rm -f "${GENERATED_CPP}" "${LIB_PATH}"

python "${SCRIPT_DIR}/kernels/fa_builder.py" > "${MLIR_PATH}"
# No --enable-insert-sync: the DSL builder inserts explicit sync primitives.
ptoas --pto-arch=a3 --enable-insert-sync "${MLIR_PATH}" > "${GENERATED_CPP}"

# Per-block GM-slot partitioning: TPipe does NOT offset the GM slot buffer by
# block_idx.  All blocks would share the same 8 GM slots, corrupting each
# other's c2v/v2c data.  We inject an offset into call_both so that each block
# gets its own 8-slot region.
#
# Offset = SLOTS_PER_BLOCK * SLOT_SIZE / sizeof(float)
#        = 8 * (S0 * max(S1_TILE, HEAD) * 4) / 4
#        = 8 * S0 * max(S1_TILE, HEAD)
#        = 8 * 32 * 256 = 65536  fp32 elements
GM_ELEMS_PER_BLOCK=$(python3 -c "
S0, HEAD, S1_TILE, SLOTS_PER_BLOCK = 32, 32, 256, 8
print(SLOTS_PER_BLOCK * S0 * max(S1_TILE, HEAD))
")
perl -pi -e "s/  cube_kernel\\(v2,/  __gm__ float* gm_per_blk = v2 + get_block_idx() * ${GM_ELEMS_PER_BLOCK};\\n  cube_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"
perl -pi -e "s/  vector_kernel\\(v2,/  vector_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"

bisheng \
    -I"${PTO_LIB_PATH}/include" \
    -fPIC -shared -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -O2 -std=c++17 \
    -Wno-macro-redefined -Wno-ignored-attributes -fstack-protector-strong \
    -xcce -Xhost-start -Xhost-end \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-stack-size=0x8000 \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-function-stack-size=0x8000 \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-record-overflow=true \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-addr-transform \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-dcci-insert-for-scalar=false \
    --npu-arch=dav-2201 -DMEMORY_BASE \
    -std=gnu++17 \
    -DKERNEL_CPP="\"${GENERATED_CPP}\"" \
    "${SCRIPT_DIR}/caller.cpp" \
    -o "${LIB_PATH}"

echo "Generated ${GENERATED_CPP}."
echo "Built ${LIB_PATH}."
```

These two lines are currently needed for a bug in addptr, see #497 
```bash
perl -pi -e "s/  cube_kernel\\(v2,/  __gm__ float* gm_per_blk = v2 + get_block_idx() * ${GM_ELEMS_PER_BLOCK};\\n  cube_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"
perl -pi -e "s/  vector_kernel\\(v2,/  vector_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"
```

### Expected behavior

the generated kernel should use all 48 vector cores on A3

### Actual behavior / error logs

No errors to show, the generated kernel matches the torch npu fused attention reference, but it is way slower:

